I farm cowpea here in the North East, and beans don't need much fertilizer like maize does — the plant feeds itself from the soil somehow, my father always said so. I save my cash and the little fertilizer I can buy for my cereal plots, not for this one. I will use seeds I kept from last harvest because they did well, and I will spray once against the pod-sucking insects because without spray the cowpea pods come out empty — every farmer here knows this. The plot is small, less than one hectare, so my younger brother and I can manage most of the work ourselves.
